items.desc: The government has deployed 240 trained inspectors to enforce meat inspection rules, with plans to make certification compulsory across the country by July 2027.

items.title: Kathmandu is going digital. Its birds and animals are paying the price
items.desc: Telecom towers, data centres, floodlights and tangled fibre networks are disrupting the habitats and natural cycle of birds and animals. Yet the ecological consequences of this expanding infrastructure remain largely unstudied.

items.title: Five takeaways from Trump’s Asia tour: cabinet feuds, Rubio love and a Kim Jong Un curveball
items.desc: As Trump prepares for high-stakes talks in China, problems at home and divisions within his administration have followed him on his Asian tour.

items.title: How India became a rice powerhouse and why it’s becoming a problem
items.desc: Advances in crop science and decades of subsidies have driven Indian rice production to record levels, but mounting surpluses are straining public finances, storage capacity and relations with competing exporters.

items.title: Kathmandu Gorkhas and Chitwan Rhinos target first Eliminator win
items.desc: Having suffered exits in their previous playoff appearances, both franchises collide in a do-or-die battle to advance to Qualifier 2.

items.title: Defending champion Lumbini Lions cruise into the final
items.desc: The Lions defeated Sudurpaschim Royals by 6 wickets in Qualifier 1 on Tuesday. Sudurpaschim, meanwhile, still have a chance to reach the final by winning Qualifier 2.

items.title: Why has Election Commission yet to update Nepali Congress leadership records?
items.desc: The commission says it is still examining documents and constitutional amendments submitted by the party, but the delay has raised questions within the Congress amid a lingering dispute over its leadership.

items.title: Flood victims occupy Nepal Electricity Authority land, erect tents
items.desc: More than 250 displaced families from Trishuli Bazar cleared the land using an excavator, accusing the government of delaying their rehabilitation.

items.title: At Nepal tax awards, finance minister raises low investment paradox
items.desc: As the government honours top taxpayers for their fiscal contributions, businesses caution that structural bottlenecks, policy instability, and market risks continue to dampen long-term investment appetite.

items.title: Millions flowed into former teacher Inam Sapkota’s account in a year
items.desc: Bank records show Rs63.1 million deposited into the fixer’s account, with large sums transferred to company accounts soon afterwards.

items.title: Shah must use his India visit to push for progress on longstanding issues
items.desc: The prime minister must firmly advance Nepal’s interests while deepening bilateral cooperation.

items.title: What Mithila’s stray bulls tell us about Nepal’s economy
items.desc: An economy built on exporting its youth and taxing its imports is not developing; it is liquidating its future.
